name: South Couloir
text: [beta] this slot often holds snow late into summer.
[hazards] Snow-filled headwall below the Thompson-Williams saddle.
[obj_haz] Firm early-season snow on steep slopes.
[gear] Ice axe and microspikes or crampons early season or when the headwall holds snow
[descent_text] Take care finding the correct break in the headwall on the way down, especially if it is snow-filled.
[turnaround] Turn back if the headwall below the saddle is hard snow or ice and you have no axe and traction, or if thunderstorms are building by early afternoon;
[pitch_detail] Often snow-filled well into summer..
[pro_tips] Go mid-July or later for a snow-free headwall.
earlierWhy: A search found no glacier on this Sawtooth class 3 route; the slot holds snow late but the text says go mid-July for a snow-free headwall.

name: Large Ear Direct
text: [overview] scramble along the feature's top to an overhung mantle and a small crevasse you can reach across.
earlierWhy: Only a small crevasse is mentioned; glacier use and snow cover unclear. | no/unsure: An area page places this Rabbit Ears in the Strawberry Mountains as a tephra pinnacle at about 8,100 ft, so the crevasse in the text is a rock feature.

name: Twin Peaks via Broads Fork
text: [approach_variants] Snow can sit in the cirque into summer.

name: Down South
text: [overview] Numerous 4th class ridge pitches, snowy or part snow and part rock, lead to the Monte Cristo south face.
[overview] One party climbed during what were basically winter conditions, using an axe and crampons on the lower pitches in mountain boots;
[overview] the face itself was bare of snow apart from some ledges.

name: Anderson Pass
text: [approach_variants] Snow, when present, only lasts into early summer, and without it the pitch is a steep walk..
[approach_variants] Snow may linger on the upper slopes into early summer.
[overview] Snow climbing up the prominent coulouir seen directly beneath the summit of Kings.
[overview] For more snow, climb the face right of the summit ridge instead.
[overview] Without snow this is a steep hike, while with snow it adds some interest to an otherwise monotonous walk.
earlierWhy: The Uintas hold rock glaciers, not crevassed ice, per the state survey; snow lasts only into early summer and the usual season is unclear.

name: The Central Spur
text: [overview] P3 (5.9, 20m): rightward under the roof, 2 bolts, then the snow ramp, ending at a fixed belay on a ledge.
[what_to_bring] ice axe or ski poles — depending on conditions
earlierWhy: No live glaciers in Utah per the state survey; the snow ramp and axe-or-poles note do not say whether snow is normal.

name: Southeast Face / South Ridge
text: [seasonal_hazards] N/A - no glacier travel on this route
[approach_variants] The mine creek is the last reliable water until lingering snow high on the peak.

[beta] From High Pass the route crosses talus, scree, and heather on Mount Larrabee's flank toward a saddle below the peak, then ascends slabby ledges and a snow gully to the base of the Great Chimney.
[obj_haz] lingering snow/moats in the gully into midsummer
[gear] ice axe for early-season snow gullies
[what_to_bring] ice axe for early-season snow in the approach gullies/traverses.

[approach] At High Pass, leave the maintained tread and follow the climbers' path north and west down to the old Gargett Mine workings (~5,400 ft) — the mine creek is the last reliable water source until you reach lingering snow patches high on the peak.
[seasonal_guidance] earlier in the window rock is drier but snow can still linger in gullies, tapering off through August into a fully dry September.

[seasonal_guidance] Route opens up as snow retreats, but lingering snow/wet rock in gullies and shaded sections is still common early in the month, and the access road may only recently have melted out.
[rappels] 2-3 rappels with a single 60 m rope through the Great Chimney and the snow gully;
earlierWhy: Text says no glacier travel; lingering snow gully to the Great Chimney base into midsummer.
